bullets.title: SpaceX acquires 800 MHz spectrum for ~$8B, positioning Starlink as 4th US mobile carrier
bullets.body: SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide 800 MHz low-band spectrum portfolio from Grain Management for ~$6–8B, enabling satellite-terrestrial hybrid mobile coverage. Telecom stocks (T, TMUS, VZ) fell 5–12% on announcement while tower REITs (CCI, SBAC, AMT) rallied 7–12% on expected new colocation demand. Analysts see SpaceX reaching ~1–7% US mobile penetration by 2030–35, primarily rural, requiring ~$5B additional capex; FCC approved Starlink's Gen2 constellation (15K satellites) the same week.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +1.2% on week but breadth at historic lows — only <30% of constituents outperformed
bullets.body: S&P 500 ended +1.2% w/w at new records but breadth was at its worst since 2005 with less than 30% of constituents outperforming (2nd percentile). Mag7 led (AMZN +4.3%, MSFT +3.4%, TSLA +3.3%, GOOGL +2.4%) while SMH fell -4.3%, Software (IGV) outperformed Semis by ~800bps. Russell 2000 fell for a 5th consecutive week (-0.9%) and 75% of S&P 500 stocks have been down since mid-August.

bullets.title: OpenAI ARR clarification: $50B Sept run-rate, $70B target by year-end 2026
bullets.body: Markets fell Thursday after FT reported OpenAI's annualized revenue was $50B as of September vs. the $70B previously signaled — confusion arose from gross vs. net revenue methodology. OpenAI subsequently clarified it expects to reach or exceed $70B annualized by year-end 2026 and is raising $30B+ at a $1.4T valuation. The scare triggered heavy selling of semis/AI stocks ($1B+ net supply on desk) before a Friday snapback; the '$400–600B AI lab ARR by end-2027' threshold needed to justify 2029 capex plans remained the key market focus.

bullets.title: Fed hiking bias intact despite Oct pause; 10-year yield at 5.24–5.35%, targeting 6%
bullets.body: Fed officials (Waller, Williams, Jefferson) pushed back on an October rate hike but the hiking direction remains intact, with markets pricing 25bp in December (74% odds) and further moves in 2027. Multiple research houses see 10-year yields at 5.25–5.50% over the next 6 months; 22V targets 6% on 10-year and 8% on 30-year. Energy prices, AI capex financing, and tariff risks are all cited as upside inflation risks. October rate-hike odds collapsed from 64% to ~18–22% during the week.

bullets.title: 3Q26 earnings season kicks off with +29.5% EPS growth expected — highest bar since 2021
bullets.body: Consensus expects 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS growth of 27–29.5% YoY with 15% operating margins (second-best quarter ever) and 12.3% revenue growth; all 11 sectors expected positive. AI infrastructure spending accounts for roughly 50% of projected growth. Large-cap banks report starting Oct 13 (C, GS, JPM, WFC). Morgan Stanley estimates median S&P 500 stock earnings growth of only 9% in Q3, down from 14% in Q2 — the top-line is highly concentrated.

bullets.title: Meta Muse tops US App Store for 22+ days; agentic AI disrupting OTAs, telecoms, marketplaces
bullets.body: Meta Muse hit #1 in the US App Store for 22+ consecutive days with 6.6M+ downloads and ~1.8M DAUs. The agent now completes full booking transactions without OTA/hotel integration, books travel independently, and negotiates telecom bills — OTA stocks (EXPE, BKNG, ABNB) fell 15–25% on the news while multiple analysts estimate Muse's LT revenue potential at $27–50B. Wolfe Research and Citi both noted that marketplace selloff fears appear overdone given only 27% of consumers have tried Muse and 64% won't trust agents with credit cards.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: Democrats favored for House (85–90%), Senate closer (55–65%); market impact seen as modest
bullets.body: Prediction markets assign >90% odds Democrats will net at least 3 House seats, and 55–65% odds for Senate. Goldman and 22V research note the policy difference between a 'Blue House' and a 'Blue Sweep' scenario is small because tariff authority, foreign policy, and deregulation remain executive-branch powers regardless of Congress. Data center buildout regulatory risk (water, permitting, moratoriums in SF, Raleigh, Oakland) is one sector where a Democratic Congress matters.

bullets.title: AI CapEx financing cycle: $400–600B ARR threshold by end-2027 is the market's key number
bullets.body: Multiple research houses (22V, JPMorgan, Goldman) frame the AI bull case as needing $400–600B in combined frontier-lab ARR exiting 2027 to justify 2029-30 capex plans; failure creates a '2029 capex cliff' risk. Compute rental pricing surged to $25–50M/MW from $10–12M six months ago — sell-side models have not captured this. Hyperscaler bond issuance now represents 14% of net new Treasury supply, and SpaceX is seeking $40B to buy Nvidia chips via Apollo-led structured debt.

bullets.title: Semis: SOX -4.3% on week, heavy HF selling; rotation from AI-infrastructure into software
bullets.body: Semis were the most net-sold industry in N. America (-1.5z) and EMEA (-3z) during the week. Hedge funds rotated out of Info Tech (sold -1.0 SDs after 4 of 5 prior weeks buying) into Industrials and Software. IGV +3.9% vs SOX -4.3% — the widest 1-week spread in recent memory. MRVL was the standout to the upside (+8% intraday at Investor Day on FY31 $70–90B revenue and $30+ EPS guidance) while INTC fell -12.3% w/w. AAPL cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max orders ~15% on soft demand.

bullets.title: LUMENTUM: optical components completely sold out through early 2029; 70% of demand unmet in 2027
bullets.body: Lumentum's CEO stated the company is completely sold out of AI server optical components through early 2029, extending the prior 2028 timeline by six months, and is unable to meet approximately 70% of demand for some products through next year. The news drove LITE +6–9% and sympathy gains across AAOI, COHR, FN, GLW, CIEN, TSEM. MRVL's Investor Day reinforced the optical theme with a $37.5B interconnect revenue target by FY31 at 60–65% CAGR.

bullets.title: IPPs surge ~15% on CEG-Google nuclear deal; AI power demand increasingly viewed as real monetizable constraint
bullets.body: Constellation Energy announced a 20-year 890 MW new nuclear PPA with Google plus a 15-year 2.7 GW existing-capacity agreement in PJM — the third major data center power deal in 2026 without a 1-for-1 new generation requirement. CEG, TLN, and VST all rallied 15–18% on the week. Power Infrastructure valuation has normalized from elevated levels and positioning is now low, with earnings revisions expected as more mega-cap tech partnerships are announced. Morgan Stanley estimates a 34% net US power shortfall through 2028.

bullets.title: Bull market turns 4 years old; breadth collapse to 47% participation raises 2027 peak risk
bullets.body: Ari Wald (Oppenheimer) notes the bull market hit its 4-year anniversary — the 6th longest since 1932 — with the SPX up 125% vs. a historical median of 73% over 32 months. Russell 3000 participation fell from 70% in August to 47%, and Russell 2000 correction reached 10%. Historical median 5th-year return is +21% (range -24% to +36%), but a breadth recovery to 60% in Q4 is described as critical to avoid a cautious 2027 outlook.

bullets.title: France/Europe sovereign stress: OAT spreads blow out, ECB TPI risk rising
bullets.body: French 10-year spreads to Germany are expected to keep widening; the French political system cannot address its fiscal challenge (govt spending >50% of GDP for 35 years) until a May election. European sovereign spreads hit ~140bps and STOXX 600 fell to a 4-month low. JPMorgan cut Euro area 3Q GDP to 1.0% annualized and Germany to just 0.25%. The EU-China trade confrontation was pushed to Q1 2027, providing modest temporary relief for European corporates.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex: Big 5 cloud capex +93% YoY in 2026, 2027 now tracking >40% growth
bullets.body: JPMorgan and Citi both revised Big Five hyperscaler aggregate capex higher to +93% YoY for 2026, with 2027 growth projections moving from >30% to >40% YoY. AWS CEO confirmed no slowdown in capex with Trainium sold out through late 2027 and GPU fulfillment only ~60%. TSMC September revenue rose 55% YoY, and Samsung 3Q operating profit was up ~9x YoY. Data center supply is forecast to grow 23% CAGR from 140 GW (2026) to 395 GW (2031).

bullets.title: CPI next Wednesday — September core expected +0.24% m/m, easing from +0.29% prior
bullets.body: Multiple desks forecast September core CPI at 0.24% m/m (2.5% YoY), down from 0.29% in August, with headline driven higher by oil/diesel to +0.5–0.6%. Piper Sandler sees September as the inflection month where goods disinflation fades and energy/services hold firm. University of Michigan 1-year inflation expectations came in at 4.7% (softer than consensus 4.8%). A hot print could push short-dated implied vol into the low 20s and trigger ~$90B of systematic equity supply.

bullets.title: HF flows: Bought US banks (2nd straight week), sold semis; net leverage near 10th percentile
bullets.body: Hedge funds bought Large Cap Banks for the second straight week (+1.5z past 5 days, near historical highs in positioning) vs. selling Regional Banks (-0.9z). Semis were the most net-sold industry globally. Overall HF equity L/S fell -0.70% vs MSCI World +0.78% during the week. Net leverage sits near the 10th percentile of the 12-month lookback. Systematic macro leverage is near the 80th 5-year percentile, limiting additional buying scope.

bullets.title: PC shipments fell 20.1% YoY in 3Q26 — worst decline since COVID; DELL, HP hit hardest
bullets.body: IDC reported 3Q26 PC shipments of 62.7M units, down 20.1% YoY and 9.1% QoQ, driven by 1H pull-forward ahead of memory price hikes leaving channels glutted. HP fell 30.9% YoY (market share -260bps), Dell -25.0% YoY, while Apple gained 90bps of share to 9.5%. PC ASPs rose ~21% YoY, partially offsetting unit weakness. Further deterioration is probable in 2H26 given worsening macro.

bullets.title: Brazil election: Bolsonaro leads runoff; JPM upgrades Brazil to OW, expects 12–20% upside
bullets.body: Flávio Bolsonaro entered the October 25 runoff with a ~6pt lead after first-round results; Polymarket assigns 82% probability of a Bolsonaro win. Right-leaning parties posted their strongest congressional showing in decades. JPMorgan upgraded Brazil equities to Overweight, targets 12% near-term and 20% medium-term MSCI upside, upgraded BRL to Overweight, and sees the Selic rate easing path opening. Brazil trades at 8.9x forward PE vs. a potential 10.9x in a positive scenario.

bullets.title: AI trade moving 'up the stack': personal agents seen as next phase after coding applications
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs and multiple firms note market focus is shifting from AI coding applications (now well-known) to personal agents as the next AI opportunity. Meta Muse's launch is exhibit A. Jefferies estimates $400–600B combined AI lab ARR by 2027 is required to sustain the capex cycle. Survey data (22V) shows 62% of investors expect mega-cap tech/AI to lead sector performance over the next 6 months, and 54% don't expect compute oversupply until 2031+.
